title: Sun-Face Buddha, Moon-Face Buddha
author: Zhiyu
excerpt: Question: In the Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Mazu Daoyi, Mazu said: “Sun-Face Buddha, Moon-Face Buddha.” What does this mean?

inline.s: Question: In the Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Mazu Daoyi, Mazu said: “Sun-Face Buddha, Moon-Face Buddha.” What does this mean?
Answer: In order to understand these two lines better, the passage is quoted below:
(the reign name of Emperor Dezong Li Kuo of the Tang dynasty)

in the middle of the first month climbed Shimen (Stone Gate) Mountain in Jianchang and walked in meditation through the forest. Seeing that a cave and ravine there were level ground, he said to his attendant: “This worn-out body of mine shall return to this place next month.” Having spoken, he turned back. Before long he showed signs of illness. The head of the monastery asked: “How has the Master’s health been lately
(zūnhòu, a respectful way of inquiring after someone’s well-being)
?” The Master said: “Sun-Face Buddha, Moon-Face Buddha.” On the first day of the second month, he bathed, sat in full lotus, and entered nirvāṇa. In the Yuanhe era
(the reign name of Emperor Xianzong Li Chun of the Tang,
, a title conferred by the emperor after death)
Chan Master Daji (Great Quiescence), and his stupa was named Dazhuangyan (Great Adornment).

by day one faces the Buddha of self-nature, and by night one faces the Buddha of self-nature. The meaning is: dwelling in one’s original nature both day and night. Chan Master Yuanwu Keqin commented on this:
‘If the Patriarch had not met people through his own fundamental concern, how could this Way have obtained such radiance?’

[Fundamental concern] the fundamental concern of a Chan practitioner, meaning to see one’s nature and awaken the mind, until one acts naturally and effortlessly. [Radiance of the Way] also called the light of the Way, the brightness of the Way: the radiance of the Way. The essence of the Way is pure, free from all faults and defilements, illuminating and dispelling the darkness of ignorance; therefore it is called the light of the Way. [Original nature] self-nature has two states, delusion and awakening. The Platform Sutra of the Sixth Patriarch says:
“When self-nature is deluded, one is a sentient being; when self-nature is awakened, one is a Buddha.”
The awakening of self-nature is the original state of self-nature, called the original nature. (On original nature, see in detail
